LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING 2.1 Independent By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners guess the m
Topic 2.2: Reading comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions 
2. use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading comprehension helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions 

What this means
In this part you learn to read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions . Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding

What this means
In this part you learn to use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions )

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading comprehension to a partner. (skill: use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions .
3. Practise this skill: use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Reading comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read through texts to make and real life personal judgments or opinions .
5. Be able to: use acquired words to form  Learners practice reading at an sentences and read them appropriate speed and with accurately at an appropriate speed understanding.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
